newsitem.title: USA: Clinton tops list of gossips' favorites.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tops list of gossips' favorites.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has a new honour on top of being U.S. chief executive -- his is the name most often mentioned in New York City's gossip columns.

His name appeared a total of 339 times this year in a dozen gossip columns, according to a survey by The New York Observer, a local weekly newspaper. In the spotlight more than ever in an election year, Clinton moved up from fourth place.
Losing Republican candidate Bob Dole placed 12th on the list, up from a remote 83rd place the year before.

Holding steady in second place for two years running was singer Madonna with 300 mentions. George magazine editor John Kennedy Jr. landed in third place with 235 mentions, but his new wife Carolyn Bessette Kennedy was in 32nd place with 86.

O.J. Simpson, last year's first place holder, slipped to fourth place, followed by New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, actress Sharon Stone, first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, actress Barbra Streisand, actor Sylvester Stallone and Britain's Princess Diana.
Diana's former sister-in-law Sarah Ferguson placed 19th, and her former husband Prince Charles tied for 35th place with model Elle Macpherson and New York Sen. Alfonse D'Amato.
The late Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis ranked 20th, largely because of highly publicised auctions of her possessions this year.

The results were culled from 12 gossip columns including Cindy Adams in the New York Post, George Rush and Joanna Molloy in the Daily News, Michael Musto in the Village Voice and syndicated columnist Liz Smith as well as columns in The New York Times, Women's Wear Daily, New Yorker magazine and New York magazine.
